section.title: Creating Vertex Form from a Vertex and a Point
section.para: Write the quadratic in vertex form that has a vertex at \((3, 4)\) and goes through the point \((1, 2)\).
First start with the vertex form of a quadratic function.

Step 1 - Substitute the vertex in at \((h, k)\).
\(y=a(x-3)^2+4\)

Step 2 - Substitute the other point at \((x, y)\).
\(2=a(1-3)^2+4\)

Step 4 - Substitute the value of \(a\) value and the vertex \((h, k)\) into the vertex form.
\(y=-\frac12(x-3)^2+4\)
section.title: Try It: Creating Vertex Form from a Vertex and a Point

div.para:
\(y=2(x-2)^2+5\)
First start with the vertex form of a quadratic function.
\(y=a(x-h)^2+k\)

Step 1 - Substitute the vertex in at \((h, k)\).
\(y=a(x-2)^2+5\)

Step 2 - Substitute the other point at \((x, y)\).
\(7=a(3-2)^2+5\)

Step 4 - Substitute the value of \(a\) value and the vertex \((h, k)\) into the vertex form.
\(y=2(x-2)^2+5\)

problem.para: Write the quadratic in vertex form that has a vertex at \((2, 5)\) and goes through the point \((3, 7)\).
